newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan Metals-Aluminium, zinc rise, others stable.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan Metals-Aluminium, zinc rise, others stable.

text.p: Taiwan aluminium and zinc prices have risen since early March while most base metal prices have held steady, local traders said on Tuesday.
Taiwan prices for aluminium ingots jumped to T$51.00 per kg from T$46.00 kg on March 3 due to rising international prices, traders said.
Prices for imported Australian zinc rose to T$42.00 per kg from T$39.00 two weeks ago, they said.
Zinc reached a 4-1/2 year high of US$1,307 a tonne on the London Metals Exchange on Monday.
Taiwan aluminium buyers said the domestic economy appeared to be recovering, but expect it will take several months before demand for aluminium products begins to respond.
"We need to wait for several more months after the local economy recovers," said a buyer at China Steel Aluminium, a subsidiary of Taiwan's China Steel Corp that plans to go public within four years.
The construction sector would need months to build up demand for more aluminium, base metal traders said.
Traders said the Taiwan aluminium import premium remained at between US$90 to US$95 CIF per tonne over the London Metals Exchange.
The value of loans extended by Taiwan banks to construction firms fell 14.96 percent in December 1996 from a year earlier, marking the 20th consecutive month of declines.
Central bank officials had attributed the flat-to-negative growth in construction loans to persistent sluggishness in the pace of Taiwan's economic recovery.
Construction remains Taiwan's top consumer of basic metals.
